spec_questions: The set-screw hole (axis Z 22.6, dia 4) leaves 0.4 mm of boss above it, under the 0.6 mm minimum wall; one diameter of edge distance puts the axis at Z 19 or lower. Is 22.6 a typing error?

The dia 5.5 dowel holes on a dia 30 circle span radius 12.25 to 17.75 and the boss radius is 13: each hole is blind over a 0.75 mm lune (1.791 mm2) under the boss, so a dowel cannot pass through. The circle needs dia 31.5 or more, or the holes must continue through the boss edge.
The keyway is on +X and the set screw on +Y, 90 degrees apart: a set screw that holds a key normally sits over it. Intended?
Dia 4 for a set screw is neither an M4 tap size (3.3) nor a size for a heat-set insert or a printed thread. Which is meant?
B1.notes: First session, kept. Every specified dimension measured on the solid (b1.json measured, b1.log). Built as written; the four questions are what I would ask before printing.

B2.notes: First session ran every solve; verdict by the second. The values above are the worse of the two supports at the finest mesh (vm and layer tension: wall face fixed; layer shear, displacement: holes fixed). converged is false because the two layer measures peak on the sharp edges where the arm sides meet the plate and double each time the element there halves (sharp_side_edges); von Mises in the root fillet did converge (1 %). With those edges given the same R3 the corner of the root carries 21.6 to 23.9 MPa, a factor of 1.88 (wall fixed) to 2.08 (holes fixed) against 2.0 (all_round_fillet_variant). Printed with layers along X the factor on tension across layers is 1.12; along Z the factor on shear between layers is 1.75 to 1.95. So no print direction shows 2.0 on all three.

B3.governing: None of the three required factors is at 2.0: the lowest is yield, 2.62, in the wall strip between the upper screw and the chord (hole walls fixed, read 2 mm from the hole). What stopped the thinning: (1) the strut, whose Euler load with pinned ends is 2.02 times its force, a floor of 2.0 that I set myself because the requirement names no buckling factor; (2) the chord at 1.2 mm, three 0.4 mm perimeters; (3) the strip, where stress goes with 1/t squared, so 3.0 mm gives 1.94 by hand and 3.2 mm would save 2 %.

B4.how_tongue_was_stabilised: two 2 x 2 x 2 mm soft pads (E 0.5 MPa), one bonded to each Y face of the tongue at Z 13 to 15 (on the tilt axis, clear of the block and of every contact face), outer faces fixed; they carry at most 0.05 N of 80
B4.valid: forces, load path and displacement: yes. block_peak_vm_mpa: no
B4.why: Contact, not a bond: at 0.08 N the tongue swings 0.444 mm through the clearance as a rigid body (0.01717 rad, hand 0.0168 to 0.0176) and rests on the two predicted lines. Reaction -80.0 N. Wall forces from free-body cuts differ by 81.0 N against 80 applied, are 1.6 % above the hand values as predicted, and hold within 0.8 % over 43,133, 88,263 and 244,072 nodes; the cut method returns 80.0 N and 800 N.mm above the slot. Pads carry 0.06 %. The block peak is a line contact on the sharp slot-mouth edge: 35, 38, 53 MPa over the three meshes, above yield, so it is not a stress; 2 mm away the peak is 8.7 MPa and the 1 mm average 17 to 21 MPa. The reverse-load run did not converge and is INVALID, not used.

reverse_load_minus_0p08N.reason: 100 contact iterations, solver reported failure to achieve equilibrium; the saved unconverged result shows wall forces of hundreds of newtons
